native_retrieval.title: What Is JEE? Eligibility Criteria, Application, and Preparation
native_retrieval.snippet: # What Is JEE? Learn important details about the Joint Entrance Examination, India’s national-level engineering entrance examination, including how to prepare. The Joint Entrance Examination (JEE) is a competitive examination required to enter some of India’s preeminent engineering universities, colleges, and institutions. If you’re considering a career in engineering, understanding the JEE  and what’s involved in preparing for it could significantly affect your performance. ## What is the JEE Exam? JEE stands for Joint Entrance Exam, a national engineering entrance examination administered by NTA. The JEE exam involves candidates who clear two examination levels: JEE (Main) and JEE (Advanced). The mission of JEE (Main) includes two testing sessions, Paper 1 and Paper 2. The objective of Paper 1 is to categorise candidates suitable for sitting in JEE (Advanced) or gaining admission to a Bachelor of Engineering (BE) or Bachelor of Technology (BTech) undergraduate programme at one of the following types of institutions:. As of 2025, the JEE (Main) entrance examination has two sessions.

native_retrieval.title: JEE Full Form
native_retrieval.snippet: ## JEE Full Form - Its Importance For Engineering Aspirants. ## Full Form of JEE and its Importance. This is a selection process for the students who want to get admission in the top engineering institutes across the world. The candidates who can successfully pass the JEE main exam can appear in the JEE advance exam. This is the first milestone that the students need to cross to get admitted to the best colleges across the country. ### What is the Importance of the JEE Exam? The key reason for this examination is to select the best students out of the rest. If you score high on the JEE exam, then you will get the chance to study in the top universities. If you pass the JEE main exam next, you will have to appear in the JEE Advanced. If you give both of these exams, you will get the chance to study in the IITs. The JEE main exam comprises Paper 1 and Paper 2.

native_retrieval.title: Joint Entrance Examination
native_retrieval.snippet: The Joint Seat Allocation Authority (JoSAA) conducts the joint admission process for a total of 23 Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs), 31 National Institutes of Technology (NITs), 25 Indian Institutes of Information Technology (IIITs) campuses and other Government Funded Technical Institutes (GFTIs) based on the rank obtained by a student in JEE–Main or JEE–Advanced, depending on the engineering college.

The **Joint Entrance Examination – Main** (**JEE–Main**), formerly **All India Engineering Entrance Examination** (**AIEEE**), is an Indian standardized computer-based test for admission to various technical undergraduate programs in engineering, architecture, and planning across colleges in India. The exam is conducted by the National Testing Agency for admission to B.Tech, B.Arch, B.Planning etc. The AIEEE was introduced in 2002, since the newly established NITs "National Institutes of Technology (India)"), IIITs and GFTIs wanted an entrance examination paper of a higher standard than the Common Engineering Test (CET), which was formerly used for admission to all non-IIT engineering colleges and some state government colleges (by a few states), including RECs and IIITs, owing mostly to the rising competition and the goal of maintaining the exclusiveness of such institutes of national importance.
